Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-03T09:12:00Z
Subject: Badge scanner failover proofing + SFDC field mapping for BrightLeaf Summit

Hi Elena,

Great talking yesterday — thanks for walking through your badge scanner topology. Per our call, I want to confirm two items before we lock schedules for the Summit (May 18–20):

1) Failover proofing: we want to validate how the kiosk behaves when network connectivity drops (offline write queue, local cache TTL, reconciliation window). Can you confirm whether your scanners currently keep badge reads locally for 48 hours or longer? If not, what's the max buffer?

2) SFDC field mapping: we need the canonical field names for lead ingestion so we can provide a CSV mapping for your ops team. Example fields we expect: email, first_name, last_name, company, badge_id, opt_in_checkbox, source_event_id, capture_timestamp, lead_owner. If you have a custom field for consent text or opt-in language, please share the API name.

Attached is a short checklist and the test plan outline we typically run on day -7 and day -1 of the event. Can Lauren and Marissa weigh in on the offline reconciliation SLAs?

Next steps I propose:
- Elena to confirm buffer TTL and share SFDC field export (by end of day Friday).
- We send a short failover test playbook and schedule a 30-minute dry run (suggest May 11).

Attachments: [Attachment: brightleaf-event-checklist.pdf (pdf)]

Thanks — happy to adjust based on your constraints.

Best,
Karthik

Date: 2027-04-03T13:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Badge scanner failover proofing + SFDC field mapping for BrightLeaf Summit

Thanks Karthik — good summary. A couple quick answers: 

• Our scanners persist reads locally for up to 72 hours before eviction; the offline queue size depends on the kiosk model but typically holds ~10k reads.
• I'll attach our current SFDC export (small sample). Our consent field is a custom checkbox named Consent__c and we store opt-in language in Consent_Text__c.

Two questions from our side:
1) For privacy, do you redact PII in the local cache prior to upload if the kiosk is ever lost?
2) Can Redwood write to a custom lead-owner routing rule in our instance (we use a territory map)?

I'll upload the SFDC sample shortly. Looping in Carlos for procurement timing — procurement will want the MAC and PO terms visible before May.

—Elena
Director, Event Operations
BrightLeaf
elena.morales@brightleaf.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@brightleaf.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-04T08:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Badge scanner failover proofing + SFDC field mapping for BrightLeaf Summit

Elena — thanks for the quick reply and the SFDC sample. A few notes below; answers inline.

1) Local cache PII: we do not redact PII in the kiosk local cache by default because we need the full record to reconcile dedupes on upload. That said, we can enable optional field-level encryption for the local store (tokenization) and a shorter TTL; that is a configuration flag in our kiosk agent. If you prefer tokenization + 48-hour TTL we'll include that in the configuration.

2) Lead owner routing: yes — Redwood can call a lead-owner upsert endpoint or write to a custom OwnerId mapping during ingestion. We typically consume your territory map file and annotate incoming leads with a routing_tag field so your SFDC rules can pick it up. We'll need a read-only API key with the appropriate mapping or a CSV of the territory rules.

Attached: scanner-failover-diagram.pdf (diagram of kiosk cache + sync flow) and sfdc-field-mapping.csv (redwood-side canonical mapping).

Proposed timeline:
- Apr 10: Confirm config (tokenization vs. no tokenization) and test account details.
- May 11: 30-minute dry run (local failure simulation + reconciliation).
- May 17: Day -1 validation on-site (connectivity checks + final sync).

Lauren / Marissa — can you confirm we have a bench environment for the dry run and whether the dry run should mirror the Summit's expected ingest rate (we have capacity planning numbers in the mapping CSV)?

Thanks,
Karthik

[Attachments: scanner-failover-diagram.pdf (pdf), sfdc-field-mapping.csv (csv)]
